html:
Iran has commenced six days of funeral ceremonies for Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, whom many headlines refer to as the martyred Leader, killed in a US-Israeli attack in February. This massive event is being framed by Iran as a potent display of national power and defiance amidst ongoing tensions and indirect discussions with the US.

Iran's Geopolitical Posture: Amid the massive funeral rites for the martyred Leader, Iran's leadership emphasizes strength and resolve. The IRGC caretaker chief Vahidi made a public appearance, and the IRGC warned of a "more crushing response" to any enemy miscalculation, with the Iranian Army asserting distrust of the enemy and a continued "state of war." This occurs as the US and Iran held separate meetings in Qatar, with "positive progress made" and an agreement to continue discussions, despite a US envoy stating Trump’s patience with Iran is "not unlimited" and Trump claiming Iran agrees to "just about everything" the US needs. Tensions persist in the Strait of Hormuz, where the IRGC is deploying special forces. Separately, a bomb blast in Damascus killed at least nine, and the US signed an agreement to build a permanent embassy in Jerusalem, drawing criticism from rights groups. Palestinians in Gaza marked 1,000 days since Israel's full-scale war, with over 73,000 Palestinians killed.

Eurasian Conflicts & Climate: Russia launched its "most massive" attack on Kyiv, deploying the largest number of weapons and killing at least 30 people, involving ballistic missiles and drones. Ukraine is receiving AI drones from German defense company Helsing. In Europe, an extreme heatwave broke June temperature records across the UK and Germany, and the French government faces a no-confidence motion over its handling of a severe heatwave that reportedly killed 1,000. In UK politics, Labour MP Andy Burnham hinted at tax flexibility, and the culture and media department stopped using X, citing abuse and misinformation.

US Internal & External Focus: Donald Trump's cryptocurrency ventures, which earned him over $1 billion last year, are raising "clear conflict of interest" concerns from a former White House ethics lawyer. Trump also declared it "ridiculous" for the US to maintain current support for NATO, ahead of an alliance summit, with reports of the US urging allies to increase defense spending for "goodies" from Trump. A scorching US heatwave, deemed "virtually impossible" without the climate crisis, threatens Independence Day celebrations and World Cup matches, as faith in the "American Dream" reportedly fades on its 250th anniversary.

Global Economy & Tech: The EU targeted Chinese imports, ending a customs exemption for low-value goods while agreeing with Beijing to monitor trade flows and improve rare earth material access. An EU lawmaker investigating surveillance was also reportedly hacked by Israeli Pegasus spyware. Globally, Instagram is running ads promoting child sexual abuse material in India, linking to Telegram. In economic news, gold prices rose over 1% on weaker US jobs data for its first weekly gain in five weeks, with the World Gold Council forecasting gold will not drop below $4,000 per ounce until the end of 2026.
